findings.description: Contention/acquisition-failure semantics is the sub-decision SHEET-PUB-004 leaves entirely open ('shall acquire... before mutating... and release it after' says nothing about what happens when acquisition is contended), and A and B resolve it in opposite directions, revealing a materially wrong 'obvious' reading. All three A sketches unanimously modeled acquisition as blocking/infallible: A1 and A2 use `Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>` with `.lock().await` (waits forever, no Err path at all); A3 uses a `WorkbookLock` trait whose `acquire_write` is documented 'Blocks until the lock is held' and returns a bare guard, not a `Result`. None of the three A implementations has any code path for 'lock is currently held' other than waiting. The REAL code (`republish` in lib.rs, lines ~954-999) is the opposite: `lock: &L where L: Lock` is `pt_core::Lock` with `fn acquire(&self) -> Result<LockGuard, LockError>` — a fallible, NON-blocking acquire. On `Err` (exercised by the test's `HeldLock`, whose `acquire()` always returns `Err(LockError::Held)`), `republish` does not wait or retry — it immediately returns `RepublishOutcome { published: false, stale_tabs: self.stale_tabs() }` (the pre-existing, unchanged stale set) having issued zero `batch_update_view`/`set_tab_order` calls, per `republish_under_a_held_lock_writes_nothing` and `republish_acquires_the_lock_before_mutating` (asserting `acquire_count() == 1`). All three B reconstructions (B1 event-driven #2, B2 E1/UB1, B3 SHEET-REPUB-LOCK-2) independently pin this exact fail-fast, non-destructive-refusal, unchanged-stale-set contract from the tests. The return-type shape tracks the same gap: all three A sketches invented `Result<(), SomeError>` + `?`-propagation (no way to report 'didn't publish, but here's the current stale set, and it's not an error'), while the real signature is an infallible `RepublishOutcome` struct precisely because 'lock held' is a normal, cheaply-recoverable outcome, not an error. A fresh implementer given only the EARS text would build a stalling/deadlocking mutex-wait exactly as A1-A3 did; the real system instead expects a caller loop that retries next sync cycle.

The real `republish_then_settle` method (and its test `every_settle_read_happens_after_all_writes_in_a_cycle`) enforces a cross-primitive ordering guarantee SHEET-PUB-004's text never states: every settle-pass `read_price_pass` call must occur strictly after every `batch_update_view`/`set_tab_order` write call of the same cycle — verified via seam call-log indices (`max(write indices) < min(read indices)`), holding even across multiple settle polls (transient→numeric). SHEET-PUB-004 only speaks to `republish` acquiring/releasing around its OWN mutation; it says nothing about a second primitive (the settle read) whose correctness depends on the lock's release boundary. B1 (state-driven #3 + ubiquitous #4), B2 (U3/U4), and B3 (LOCK-4/LOCK-5) all pin this identically, quoting the same index-ordering fact. No A output touches this since A was scoped to `republish` alone, not `republish_then_settle`.

Exact acquisition cardinality — 'exactly once per republish call, covering the whole tab batch plus the `set_tab_order` reassert, not once per tab' — is pinned by all three B outputs from `acquire_count() == 1` in `republish_acquires_the_lock_before_mutating`, a level of precision the spec text ('acquire the... lock before mutating') doesn't itself force (it's silent on granularity). Not a drift against A here (A1-A3 also guessed whole-batch scope correctly), but it is B-side surplus worth naming: the spec is compatible with per-tab acquire/release too, and only the test rules that out.

B1 alone reconstructs a materially larger, adjacent requirement set under the same 'lock coordination' heading — per-tab failure isolation (one tab's `batch_update_view` failure doesn't abort the others), the exact best-effort banner text "STALE — last sync {ts}", swallowed banner-write failures, and stale-set clear-on-next-success — none of which SHEET-PUB-004's text addresses (it's a separate concern, almost certainly a different SHEET-PUB EARS id). B2 and B3 stay tightly scoped to the lock itself. This is real, test-pinned behavior, so not wrong, but it's a scope-breadth disagreement internal to the B runs rather than an A/B drift.

notes: Checked the real republish() in crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs (~lines 954-999) and its tests in tests/republish.rs. The literal explicit clause of SHEET-PUB-004 ('acquire before mutating, release after, so republish never writes concurrently with another Sheets-mutating primitive') IS honored by the real code — guard acquired before the tab loop, held through set_tab_order, released on scope exit (RAII), and a held lock never lets two writers run concurrently. So there is no bare A-side-surplus finding of the strict 'spec states X, code lacks X' type; the drift is entirely in the *sub-decision the spec leaves open* (contention/failure behavior) that A unanimously resolves one way (blocking/infallible, tokio-async in A1/A2, blocking-trait in A3) and the real code resolves the opposite way (fallible, fail-fast, non-blocking), independently confirmed by all three B reconstructions via the HeldLock test. That is the strongest, cleanly-BD finding. A's internal split between tokio-async (A1/A2) vs a synchronous blocking trait (A3) is a technology-choice disagreement, not a behavioral one (both still assume 'wait until acquired'), so aAgreement is rated high on substance. bAgreement is high on the core lock semantics (all three cite the same tests/constants); the only B-internal wrinkle is B1's much broader scope pulling in unrelated per-tab/banner requirements.
